Today, Thermo Fisher Scientific and Mayo Clinic announced the launch of Precure, LLC, designed to help researchers better understand the biological changes that occur before symptoms of disease appear.

Precure will bring together genomic and proteomic data generated from one million biospecimens with health information collected over time, creating one of the world’s leading biomedical datasets. Using advanced AI and large-scale data analytics, researchers will be able to identify patterns at significant scale, with the potential to deepen understanding of disease biology, accelerate drug development and create new opportunities for earlier diagnosis, intervention and more personalized care.

The research will span major health conditions, such as cancer, cardiometabolic disease, neurological disorders and immune-mediated disease.

By combining our industry-leading proteomics expertise and solutions with Mayo Clinic’s world-class clinical and research leadership, we’re helping create a powerful resource to help researchers uncover new insights into how disease develops and translate those discoveries into meaningful advances for patients.

Together, we’re advancing science that can help make the world healthier. 

Learn more: https://lnkd.in/eAXp5nEn

Medicines used around the world depend on the expertise of people who know how to turn scientific ideas into reliable manufacturing.

Austrian Federal Minister for Economy, Energy and Tourism Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer and Federal Minister for Women, Science and Research Eva-Maria Holzleitner visited our site in Linz, Austria, to meet the colleagues helping pharmaceutical companies develop and manufacture the ingredients that go into medicines.

Our team shared how we work alongside customers at every stage, from developing reliable ways to make these ingredients to producing them at scale. This work also helps strengthen pharmaceutical manufacturing, scientific innovation and reliable supply chains in Austria and beyond.

Thank you, Minister Hattmannsdorfer and Minister Holzleitner, for spending time with our colleagues and learning more about the work happening in Linz to support medicines for patients around the world.

30 young innovators. Big questions. Ideas that could shape the future.

Meet the finalists of the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.

These middle school scientists and engineers are tackling real-world challenges — from kelp forest recovery and wildfire risk to traumatic brain injury and the way language shapes conversations on social media.

Representing 17 states and Puerto Rico, the finalists will head to Washington, D.C. in October to put their research, creativity and collaboration skills to the test while competing for more than $100,000 in awards.

As our Chief Scientific Officer Karen Nelson shared, “We hope they walk away from Finals Week more confident in their own ideas, inspired by their peers and motivated to examine the challenges they encounter in their daily lives through the lens of science.”

Together with Society for Science, we’re helping give young innovators the opportunity to follow their curiosity, challenge assumptions and see just how far their ideas can go.

Learn more: https://lnkd.in/eYCRYhnZ
